# Thematic Analysis of Interview Excerpts

---

## COHORT 1: `transit_primary` — Main Themes

---

### Theme T1: Real-Time Information Accuracy & Trust
**Description:** Respondents place high value on the reliability of live data. When real-time information is incorrect or vague, it erodes trust and has cascading consequences for their journeys. Honest, specific communication is preferred over generic updates.

> *"The live arrival board is what I open first; when it is wrong I miss connections and the rest of my day slides sideways."* — INT-01

> *"Delays are fine if the explanation is honest—generic delays erode trust faster than a long wait with a reason."* — INT-08

**Respondents:** INT-01, INT-08

---

### Theme T2: Crowding, Safety & Physical Comfort
**Description:** Perceived physical safety on platforms and vehicles influences decision-making independently of schedule accuracy. Respondents make active trade-offs — skipping on-time trains — when crowding feels unsafe, suggesting that capacity data is as important as timing data.

> *"Sometimes I skip a train even if the app says it is on time because I know the platform will be unsafe."* — INT-02

**Respondents:** INT-02

---

### Theme T3: Pricing Transparency & Financial Clarity
**Description:** Fare structures are experienced as unnecessarily complex and hidden behind multiple navigation layers. Respondents want consolidated, surfaced cost information without having to actively search for it.

> *"Pricing feels opaque; I want a single place that shows weekly caps and discounts without digging through three menus."* — INT-03

**Respondents:** INT-03

---

### Theme T4: Safety & Confidence During Off-Peak / Night Travel
**Description:** Service gaps during late hours create anxiety. Respondents expect the app to proactively bridge these gaps — for example, by pairing last-service information with onward navigation — rather than leaving users to problem-solve alone in vulnerable situations.

> *"Night service gaps are scary; the app should pair walking directions with the last train so I am not guessing alone at midnight."* — INT-04

**Respondents:** INT-04

---

### Theme T5: Accessibility Information Visibility
**Description:** Critical accessibility data (e.g., elevator outages) is deprioritised in the interface relative to promotional content. Respondents with accessibility needs experience this as a significant failure of information hierarchy.

> *"Elevator outages are buried; I need that louder than marketing banners."* — INT-05

**Respondents:** INT-05

---

### Theme T6: Offline Functionality & Connectivity Resilience
**Description:** Transit environments (tunnels, underground stations) frequently disrupt connectivity. Offline capability is not seen as a bonus feature but as a core retention driver — its absence is a switching trigger.

> *"That single feature keeps me from switching apps."* — INT-06

**Respondents:** INT-06

---

### Theme T7: Transfer Complexity & Navigation Coherence
**Description:** Multi-line transfers within the same physical station are undermined by inconsistent naming conventions across lines. The map fails to reconcile these discrepancies, creating confusion at a critical decision point in the journey.

> *"Same station but different names across lines and the map does not reconcile them."* — INT-07

**Respondents:** INT-07

---

### Theme T8: Multimodal Integration & Last-Mile Connectivity
**Description:** Respondents expect the app to extend its routing logic beyond the transit network to include last-mile options (e.g., bike-share) anchored to the specific exit they use, not a generic street-level approximation.

> *"I wish the app surfaced bike-share docks near the exit I actually use; routing assumes a generic street corner."* — INT-09

**Respondents:** INT-09

---
---

## COHORT 2: `car_primary` — Main Themes

---

### Theme C1: Integrated Cost Visibility Across Modes
**Description:** Car-primary users make modal decisions based on total cost, but the app presents driving costs (particularly parking) in isolation from other relevant data. Respondents want a unified cost view to support informed, real-time decision-making.

> *"The app's drive-time estimate helps me decide but parking costs are never in the same view."* — INT-10

> *"Fuel vs fare comparison would help families like mine decide weekly; right now it is guesswork across spreadsheets."* — INT-15

**Respondents:** INT-10, INT-15

---

### Theme C2: Alert Relevance & Notification Fatigue
**Description:** Traffic alerts are valued in principle but experienced as poorly calibrated. Respondents apply their own cost-benefit logic (delay vs. parking search time) that the app does not replicate, resulting in alerts that feel noisy rather than actionable.

> *"I only want reroutes when the delay exceeds what I would lose searching for parking."* — INT-11

**Respondents:** INT-11

---

### Theme C3: Seamless Park-and-Ride / Multimodal Trip Stitching
**Description:** Respondents who combine driving with transit experience a fundamental structural gap: the app treats each leg as a discrete trip rather than components of a single journey. This forces manual coordination and undermines the app's utility for hybrid commuters.

> *"The app should stitch driving legs with train legs instead of treating them as separate trips."* — INT-12

**Respondents:** INT-12

---

### Theme C4: Parking Safety & Qualitative Lot Information
**Description:** Price optimisation alone is insufficient for parking decisions. Respondents factor in environmental safety attributes (lighting, surveillance) that are absent from the app, indicating that the current data model is too narrow for real-world decision-making.

> *"I want lighting and CCTV notes not just cheapest price."* — INT-13

**Respondents:** INT-13

---

### Theme C5: Feature Relevance & Personalisation of Prompts
**Description:** App-generated suggestions (e.g., carpool matching) are dismissed when they fail to respect fixed user constraints. Respondents signal that irrelevant prompts actively degrade the experience and are habitually ignored.

> *"Carpool matching is gimmicky unless it respects my fixed drop-off time; otherwise I ignore those prompts."* — INT-14

**Respondents:** INT-14

---

### Theme C6: Interface Simplicity & Cognitive Load
**Description:** The home screen is experienced as cluttered and cognitively demanding. Car-primary users, who may be consulting the app while managing a drive, have a particularly low tolerance for interface complexity and want radical prioritisation of core functions.

> *"I only need three buttons on the home screen and everything else feels like clutter."* — INT-16

**Respondents:** INT-16

---

### Theme C7: Crisis Communication & Disruption Clarity
**Description:** During major service disruptions (e.g., strikes), respondents need a single, prominent, actionable communication — not content buried within a general news feed. The app's failure to surface this clearly forces users to seek information elsewhere.

> *"I need a single banner that explains alternatives—not a feed of unrelated news."* — INT-17

**Respondents:** INT-17

---

### Theme C8: Map Accuracy as a Proxy for System Trust
**Description:** The visual map layer carries disproportionate weight in establishing overall app credibility. An inaccurate map line invalidates the entire trip plan in the user's perception, suggesting that map fidelity is a foundational trust signal.

> *"If the line on the map is wrong I assume the whole trip plan is wrong."* — INT-18

**Respondents:** INT-18

---
---

## CROSS-COHORT OVERLAPPING THEMES

---

### Theme X1: Trust, Accuracy & Credibility of Information
**Description:** Both cohorts anchor their trust in the app to the accuracy of a specific data layer — live arrivals for transit users, the map for car users. In both cases, a single point of inaccuracy is sufficient to undermine confidence in the entire system. This suggests a shared underlying need: **reliable, verifiable data as the non-negotiable foundation of app utility.**

| Cohort | Respondent | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| `transit_primary` | INT-01 | Inaccurate arrival board causes missed connections |
| `transit_primary` | INT-08 | Vague delay messaging erodes trust more than the delay itself |
| `car_primary` | INT-18 | Incorrect map line invalidates the whole trip plan |

---

### Theme X2: Multimodal Integration & Journey Continuity
**Description:** Both cohorts express frustration that the app treats modes as siloed rather than as components of a single, continuous journey. Transit users want last-mile options (bike-share, walking) stitched to their exit point; car users want driving and transit legs unified into one trip plan. The underlying need is identical: **end-to-end journey coherence across modes.**

| Cohort | Respondent | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| `transit_primary` | INT-09 | Bike-share docks should be surfaced near the actual exit used |
| `car_primary` | INT-12 | Driving and train legs should be stitched into one trip |

---

### Theme X3: Safety as a Primary Decision Factor
**Description:** Safety concerns shape behaviour in both cohorts, though the context differs. Transit users are concerned about platform crowding and late-night vulnerability; car users are concerned about parking lot safety. In both cases, **safety information is either absent or insufficiently prominent**, and its absence leads to suboptimal or anxiety-driven decisions.

| Cohort | Respondent | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| `transit_primary` | INT-02 | Skips on-time trains due to unsafe crowding |
| `transit_primary` | INT-04 | Feels unsafe navigating night service gaps without app support |
| `car_primary` | INT-13 | Prioritises lighting/CCTV over cheapest parking price |

---

### Theme X4: Disruption Communication & Proactive Alerting
**Description:** Both cohorts want the app to communicate disruptions clearly, proactively, and with actionable alternatives — not buried in feeds or absent entirely. The shared expectation is that **the app should anticipate the user's next question during a disruption and answer it immediately.**

| Cohort | Respondent | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| `transit_primary` | INT-08 | Wants honest, specific delay explanations |
| `car_primary` | INT-17 | Wants a single prominent banner with alternatives during strikes |

---

### Theme X5: Cost Transparency & Financial Decision Support
**Description:** Both cohorts want clearer, more consolidated cost information to support modal and route decisions. Transit users want fare caps and discounts surfaced; car users want parking costs and fuel-vs-fare comparisons integrated. The shared need is **cost visibility at the point of decision, without requiring the user to aggregate data manually.**

| Cohort | Respondent | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| `transit_primary` | INT-03 | Weekly caps and discounts buried across menus |
| `car_primary` | INT-10 | Parking costs absent from the drive-time decision view |
| `car_primary` | INT-15 | Fuel vs. fare comparison requires manual spreadsheet work |

---

## Summary Matrix

| Theme | `transit_primary` | `car_primary` | Cross-Cohort |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Real-Time Data Accuracy & Trust | ✅ T1 | ✅ C8 | ✅ X1 |
| Crowding / Physical Comfort | ✅ T2 | — | — |
| Pricing / Cost Transparency | ✅ T3 | ✅ C1 | ✅ X5 |
| Night / Off-Peak Safety | ✅ T4 | — | — |
| Accessibility Information | ✅ T5 | — | — |
| Offline / Connectivity Resilience | ✅ T6 | — | — |
| Transfer & Navigation Coherence | ✅ T7 | — | — |
| Multimodal / Last-Mile Integration | ✅ T8 | ✅ C3 | ✅ X2 |
| Safety (Crowding / Parking / Night) | ✅ T2, T4 | ✅ C4 | ✅ X3 |
| Alert Relevance / Notification Fatigue | — | ✅ C2 | — |
| Parking Safety & Qualitative Data | — | ✅ C4 | — |
| Feature Relevance & Personalisation | — | ✅ C5 | — |
| Interface Simplicity / Cognitive Load | — | ✅ C6 | — |
| Disruption Communication | ✅ T8 (implied) | ✅ C7 | ✅ X4 |
| Map Fidelity as Trust Signal | — | ✅ C8 | — |
